text: The carpenter joined the political cabinet, bringing his own shelves.
reading_b: a piece of furniture for storage
annotation_note: The political setting and the shelves deliberately connect two readings of the same spelling.

text: The carpenter fitted adjustable shelves inside the storage cabinet.
reading_a: a piece of furniture for storage
annotation_note: Only the furniture reading is supported; a second dictionary sense is not contextual evidence.

text: The diplomat opened a new channel, then asked the plumber to inspect it.
annotation_note: The diplomatic action and the plumber's inspection create the intended change of reading.

text: The plumber inspected the drainage channel before connecting the outlet pipe.
annotation_note: Both clauses support the same physical passage; communication is not invoked.

text: Bookcase: a suitcase reserved for novels.
annotation_note: The whole word and its two concatenating parts support the intended resegmentation; no sound substitution is needed.

text: Bookcase: a cabinet with shelves for storing books.
annotation_note: The definition describes the conventional whole-word meaning; separable dictionary parts alone do not make it wordplay.

text: The director complained about the cast, so the prop maker brought a bucket of plaster.
reading_b: an object formed in a mold
annotation_note: The director's complaint and the plaster response deliberately connect acting and molding.

text: The director thanked the cast after the final rehearsal.
annotation_note: Only the performance context is supplied; material for molding is absent.
The fragment does not resolve which dictionary reading is intended; uncertainty should not be silently converted into a decision.

text: The clockmaker named the herb garden Thyme After Thyme.
reading_b: time, through a different spelling with the same sound
annotation_note: The proposed second reading requires a spelling change; it is outside the supported homographic and concatenating split mechanisms.
